snippets.headline: Blood sugar compliance includes moderate control, whereas good control and poor control apply different thresholds across all eligible patients.
snippets.content: GSD, Glycemic Status Assessment, covers diabetics aged 18–75 and uses the last A1c of the measurement year in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd. GSD compliance, also called Blood Sugar Controlled, GSD rate, or blood sugar controlled rate, is COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value <= 9.0) / COUNT(*). Good Control Rate, also called good glycemic control or controlled diabetes, is COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value < 8.0) / COUNT(*). Poor Control Rate, also called poor glycemic control or uncontrolled diabetes, is COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value > 9.0 OR gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_datetime IS NULL) / COUNT(*). Each denominator is all eligible patient rows in the selected scope, not only tested patients; missing tests are not compliant. Compliance and good control answer different questions because the former includes A1c values from 8.0 through 9.0.

snippets.headline: Good and poor glycemic control rates measure tested patients, whereas glycemic assessment compliance measures testing among all eligible patients.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: On eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd, good control is COUNT_IF(evidence_value < 8.0) / COUNT_IF(evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL), and poor control is COUNT_IF(evidence_value > 9.0) / COUNT_IF(evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL). Both denominators count A1c-tested patient rows, unlike GSD compliance's COUNT(*) eligible-row denominator. Average latest A1c (%) is AVG(evidence_value); the supplied expression has no explicit evidence_datetime filter. The clinic example also reports COUNT(*) AS eligible_patients and COUNT_IF(evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL) / COUNT(*) AS gsd_compliance_rate, GROUP BY clinic_id ORDER BY gsd_compliance_rate DESC, without a year filter. The verified poor-control sample uses MEASURE(`Poor Control Rate`) from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics. The poorly controlled patient filter INCLUDES evidence_value > 9.0.

snippets.headline: Glycemic assessment compliance measures annual testing among eligible diabetic adults, rather than whether their blood sugar is controlled.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: GSD means Glycemic Status Assessment: diabetics aged 18-75 with an A1c test in the measurement year. Patient-level clinic/panel compliance is COUNT_IF(evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL) / COUNT(*) over eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd, with all patient rows in the breakdown as denominator. Care gaps INCLUDE evidence_datetime IS NULL. This testing rate differs from good and poor control rates, whose denominator is A1c-tested patients rather than all eligible patient rows.

snippets.headline: Poor control patients count A1c-tested patients whose latest measurement-year A1c exceeds 9.0 percent.
snippets.content: On `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics`, `Poor Control Patients` is a predefined measure with definition-time expression `COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value > 9.0)` over the source. It represents patients whose latest measurement-year A1c is `> 9.0%`; the threshold is strict, so exactly 9.0 is not included. Query it as `MEASURE(`Poor Control Patients`)`, for example `SELECT `Clinic`, MEASURE(`Poor Control Patients`) AS `poor_control_patients` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics` GROUP BY ALL`.

snippets.headline: Patient-level A1c results classify patients into no-result, good-control, poor-control, or intermediate-control bands.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: The patient-level GSD A1c control band is derived from `gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value`. Use this exact expression: `CASE WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value IS NULL THEN 'No A1c' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value < 8 THEN 'Good control (<8%)' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value > 9 THEN 'Poor control (>9%)' ELSE '8-9%' END`. A missing value means `No A1c`; values below 8 are `Good control (<8%)`; values above 9 are `Poor control (>9%)`; all remaining non-null values, including 8 and 9, are `8-9%`.

snippets.headline: This metric view measures whether high A1c results receive timely follow-up, revealing protocol adherence by clinic and primary-care panel.
snippets.content: `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.protocol_adherence_metrics` is a Diabetes care-protocol Step 3 metrics view. The business question is whether an A1c result >= 9% (poor control) receives a follow-up A1c within 90 days; it is HEDIS-aligned for demonstration and is not NCQA-certified. Query the exposed dimensions and measures from this metrics view rather than treating it as a raw-row table, and use `MEASURE()` for every measure with `GROUP BY ALL`. snippets.headline: Blood sugar care gaps include both untested patients and patients above nine percent, unlike the tested poor control filter.
snippets.content: In eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd, the tested 'poor control' filter INCLUDES evidence_value > 9.0. The broader 'GSD gaps' filter INCLUDES evidence_value > 9.0 OR evidence_datetime IS NULL; its count is COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_datetime IS NULL OR gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value > 9.0). The 'no A1c' filter INCLUDES evidence_datetime IS NULL only. The text paragraph describes GSD gold-table gaps using evidence_datetime IS NULL, while the structured GSD gap snippets explicitly include high A1c as well. These scopes distinguish missing testing, tested poor control, and all GSD care gaps.

snippets.headline: Glycemic gaps distinguish missing A1c testing from a latest A1c result above nine percent.

## What drives each clinic's rate

Most poor-control patients had **no A1c test** (618 of 877 overall, \~70%). The remaining 259 had a last A1c above 9%. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/d3d22ccffb6d4052b7059b8c6955bf11?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_98ef81)

- **CLINIC-06 (39.7%)** — highest rate. 78 untested + 30 with A1c > 9% out of 272 eligible. The gap is driven primarily by untested patients.
- **CLINIC-08 (38.3%)** — 72 untested + 39 with A1c > 9% out of 290. Has the most patients with a last A1c above 9%, so the problem is more about glycemic control than testing gaps.
- **CLINIC-04 (37.9%)** — 79 untested + 35 with A1c > 9% out of 301.
- **CLINIC-03 (35.7%)** — 94 untested (the most of any clinic) + only 28 with A1c > 9% out of 342. Its problem is overwhelmingly testing gaps.
- **CLINIC-05 (32.6%)** — best performer. 66 untested + 31 with A1c > 9% out of 298. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/d3d22ccffb6d4052b7059b8c6955bf11?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_ae405e)

## Scope and definition

- **Poor control** = last A1c of the measurement year is above 9.0%, **or** no A1c test. Denominator is all eligible diabetes patients aged 18–75. Lower is better. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-788eac61-11a7-482a-9d5c-eac964e04174) [GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment for Patients With Diabetes](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/09e5fd5b-c4ed-42a7-bf34-a009c6771444?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- **Date cutoff:** the data runs through 2026-10-30; the year isn't over, so some currently-untested patients may still get tested, and rates may improve by year-end. [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol/gold_adherence_gsd?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- This repeats the same analysis from a prior run, re-executed on current data. [GSD poor-control by clinic](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/f0c13bffeb4b493296f850afa936eee2?o=7474653847172668)
- This is synthetic demo data, HEDIS-aligned but not NCQA-certified. Hospice, ESRD, and frailty exclusions are not applied, so denominators may run slightly high. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-5b26413f-23e8-4fe9-913f-c627f2cb9307)

SELECT
  `clinic_id`,
  COUNT(*) AS eligible_patients,
  COUNT_IF(`evidence_value` > 9.0 OR `evidence_datetime` IS NULL) AS poor_control_patients,
  COUNT_IF(`evidence_datetime` IS NULL) AS no_a1c_test,
  COUNT_IF(`evidence_value` > 9.0) AS a1c_above_9,
  ROUND(COUNT_IF(`evidence_value` > 9.0 OR `evidence_datetime` IS NULL) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS poor_control_rate_pct
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_gsd`
WHERE `measurement_year` = 2026
GROUP BY `clinic_id`
ORDER BY poor_control_rate_pct DESC

SELECT
  'ALL CLINICS' AS scope,
  COUNT(*) AS eligible_patients,
  COUNT_IF(`evidence_value` > 9.0 OR `evidence_datetime` IS NULL) AS poor_control_patients,
  COUNT_IF(`evidence_datetime` IS NULL) AS no_a1c_test,
  COUNT_IF(`evidence_value` > 9.0) AS a1c_above_9,
  ROUND(COUNT_IF(`evidence_value` > 9.0 OR `evidence_datetime` IS NULL) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS poor_control_rate_pct
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_gsd`
WHERE `measurement_year` = 2026

### Definitions Used

- **A1c above 9%**: the patient's last A1c of MY2026 is strictly above 9.0% — the GSD poor-control threshold. A result of exactly 9.0% does not count. Patients with no A1c test are excluded since they have no A1c above 9%. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-788eac61-11a7-482a-9d5c-eac964e04174) [GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment for Patients With Diabetes](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/09e5fd5b-c4ed-42a7-bf34-a009c6771444?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- **No statin**: the patient has no statin dispensed in MY2026 in the SPD statin-therapy measure data (through 2026-10-30). Statins are matched from drug ingredients to specific products ordered via RxNorm subsumption. Every GSD patient aged 65–75 also appears in the SPD data, since SPD covers ages 40–75. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-7408a2b2-dea4-490f-ab3c-0f41d8901eca) [SPD — Statin Therapy for Patients With Diabetes](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/c8324591-625b-44db-9f8b-c57e9ba5dd7b?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

[Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/f9b5bb3b63ed467894e368fbdd3bce4e?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_b4fbc0)

**Caveat:** This is synthetic data following HEDIS rules but is not NCQA-certified. Hospice, ESRD, frailty, and contraindication exclusions are not applied, so the count may run slightly high. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-5b26413f-23e8-4fe9-913f-c627f2cb9307)

SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_gsd` g
JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_spd` s
  ON g.`patient_id` = s.`patient_id`
  AND s.`measurement_year` = 2026
WHERE g.`measurement_year` = 2026
  AND g.`age` BETWEEN 65 AND 75
  AND g.`evidence_datetime` <= '2026-10-30 23:59:59'
  AND g.`evidence_value` > 9.0
  AND (s.`evidence_datetime` IS NULL OR s.`evidence_datetime` > '2026-10-30 23:59:59')

-- Check A1c records on 2026-10-30 with time > 00:00:00 for the relevant population
SELECT g.`patient_id`, g.`evidence_datetime`, g.`evidence_value`
FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_gsd` g
WHERE g.`measurement_year` = 2026
  AND g.`age` BETWEEN 65 AND 75
  AND g.`evidence_value` > 9.0
  AND CAST(g.`evidence_datetime` AS DATE) = '2026-10-30'
  AND g.`evidence_datetime` > '2026-10-30 00:00:00'
ORDER BY g.`evidence_datetime`

SELECT COUNT(*) AS gsd_not_in_spd

WHERE g.`measurement_year` = 2026
  AND g.`age` BETWEEN 65 AND 75
  AND s.`patient_id` IS NULL

SELECT 
  (SELECT MAX(`evidence_datetime`) FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_gsd` WHERE `measurement_year` = 2026) AS max_a1c_dt,
  (SELECT MAX(`evidence_datetime`) FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_spd` WHERE `measurement_year` = 2026) AS max_statin_dt,

snippets.headline: The target population consists of distinct patients with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure diagnoses.
snippets.content: The clinical cohort is the set of DISTINCT `patient_id` values appearing in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx` under all three diagnosis conditions: `icd10_code LIKE 'E11%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E10%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E13%'` for diabetes, `icd10_code LIKE 'N18%'` for chronic kidney disease, and `icd10_code LIKE 'I50%'` for heart failure. The three diagnosis subsets are joined with INNER JOIN on `patient_id`, so a patient must have at least one matching diagnosis in each subset. The cohort count is `COUNT(*)` over the resulting distinct patient list, not a count of diagnosis records.

snippets.headline: The cardiorenal cohort requires recorded diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure together, using diagnosis hierarchy descendants for each condition.
snippets.content: Obtain diagnosis membership from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition by semijoin membership icd10_code IN (SELECT descendant_code FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure WHERE ancestor_code IN ('E10','E11','E13')) for diabetes. snippets.headline: The cardiorenal cohort requires diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure diagnoses for the same patient.
snippets.content: The cardiorenal patient count is the number of distinct patients present in all three diagnosis cohorts: diabetes, CKD, and heart failure. Diabetes is defined by `icd10_code RLIKE '^E1[013]'`, heart failure by `icd10_code LIKE 'I50%'`, and CKD by either the direct-prefix cohort or the closure-based cohort described separately. The query computes `COUNT(*)` after joining the already-distinct patient sets with `JOIN ... USING(patient_id)`, producing `cardiorenal_prefix` for diabetes intersected with direct-prefix CKD and heart failure, and `cardiorenal_closure` for diabetes intersected with closure-based CKD and heart failure. Because each cohort is deduplicated to one row per patient before joining, the intersection counts are patient counts rather than diagnosis-row counts.

snippets.headline: Cardiorenal patients have diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure diagnoses documented through specified diagnosis-code families.
snippets.content: A cardiorenal patient is defined by all three diagnosis flags being present in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition for the same patient_id: at least one icd10_code LIKE 'E10%', 'E11%', or 'E13%' for diabetes, at least one icd10_code LIKE 'N18%' for chronic kidney disease, and at least one icd10_code LIKE 'I50%' for heart failure. Each flag is computed with MAX(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) grouped by patient_id, and the final cohort requires has_dm = 1 AND has_ckd = 1 AND has_hf = 1. These diagnosis families are inclusion criteria for the cardiorenal cohort, not merely descriptive labels.

snippets.headline: The cardio-renal diabetes cohort includes patients with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure diagnoses together.
snippets.content: The cardio-renal diabetes cohort is defined from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx at the distinct `patient_id` grain. A patient is INCLUDED only when they have at least one diagnosis code matching each of these three required groups: diabetes `icd10_code LIKE 'E11%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E10%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E13%'`, chronic kidney disease `icd10_code LIKE 'N18%'`, and heart failure `icd10_code LIKE 'I50%'`. The cohort is still the intersection of all three distinct `patient_id` sets, joined on `patient_id`. snippets.content: For each clinic, the complication share is `ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN comp.patient_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END), 3)`, where the denominator is the number of distinct `(patient_id, clinic_id)` rows from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_protocol_adherence` for `measurement_year = :my`. `patients` is `COUNT(*)` at that same clinic-scoped patient-row grain. Because the complication set is deduplicated by patient before the left join, a patient contributes 1.0 to every adherence clinic row when that patient has a qualifying complication; patients without a match contribute 0.0.

snippets.headline: Qualifying complications include diabetes kidney, eye, and other specified complication descendants under nine explicitly listed ancestor codes.
snippets.content: A patient is classified as having a qualifying complication when `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition` contains an `icd10_code` whose closure match in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure` has `ancestor_code IN ('E11.2','E10.2','E13.2','E11.3','E10.3','E13.3','E11.4','E10.4','E13.4')`. The full included ancestor-code list is exactly `('E11.2','E10.2','E13.2','E11.3','E10.3','E13.3','E11.4','E10.4','E13.4')`; no other ancestor codes are included by this rule. The complication cohort is deduplicated with `SELECT DISTINCT c.patient_id` before it is used in the clinic metric.

snippets.headline: Qualifying complications include diabetes kidney, eye, and other specified complication descendants under nine explicitly listed ancestor codes.
snippets.content: A patient is classified as having a qualifying complication when `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition` contains an `icd10_code` whose closure match in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure` has `ancestor_code IN ('E11.2','E10.2','E13.2','E11.3','E10.3','E13.3','E11.4','E10.4','E13.4')`. The full included ancestor-code list is exactly `('E11.2','E10.2','E13.2','E11.3','E10.3','E13.3','E11.4','E10.4','E13.4')`; no other ancestor codes are included by this rule. The complication cohort is deduplicated with `SELECT DISTINCT c.patient_id` before it is used in the clinic metric.

snippets.headline: Kidney-related patient counts include conditions descending from three specified diabetes kidney-disease ancestor codes.
snippets.content: Count kidney-related patients with `COUNT(DISTINCT c.patient_id)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition c` joined to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure cl` on `c.icd10_code = cl.descendant_code`. Include only closure rows where `cl.ancestor_code IN ('E11.2','E10.2','E13.2')`. The result is patient-distinct across all matching descendant conditions, not a count of condition records.

snippets.headline: The cardiorenal cohort requires recorded diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure together, using diagnosis hierarchy descendants for each condition.
snippets.content: Obtain diagnosis membership from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition by semijoin membership icd10_code IN (SELECT descendant_code FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure WHERE ancestor_code IN ('E10','E11','E13')) for diabetes. Chronic kidney disease uses ancestor_code = 'N18' and heart failure uses ancestor_code = 'I50', with the same icd10_code-to-descendant_code membership path. SELECT DISTINCT patient_id for each condition and INTERSECT all three sets, requiring every condition rather than their union. Membership semijoins do not multiply condition rows with duplicate closure matches, and deduplication yields one cohort row per patient. No diagnosis-date or active-condition filter is applied.

snippets.headline: Diabetes cohort membership includes every diagnosis subsumed by the three specified diabetes ancestors, counting each descendant code once.
snippets.content: In eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure, INCLUDE ancestor_code IN ('E10','E11','E13') for the diabetes code cohort. Its size is COUNT(DISTINCT descendant_code), not a patient count. Membership for a supplied diagnosis is COUNT(*) > 0 with the same ancestor filter and descendant_code equal to the quoted diagnosis code. The E11.21 example applies this membership test; codes are strings.

snippets.headline: Direct hierarchy edges describe one level, whereas precomputed closures describe all depths beneath a selected clinical concept.
snippets.content: eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_hier and eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_hier contain direct parent/child edges. eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure and eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure contain precomputed transitive relationships: filter ancestor_code by equality to find narrower descendant_code values at all depths. For Type 2 diabetes, direct children use icd10_hier.parent_code = 'E11', returning code and name; all-depth results use icd10_closure.ancestor_code = 'E11', returning descendant_code and descendant_name. Proper descendants, labeled 'subtypes' or 'children' in the closure filter, INCLUDE icd10_closure.depth > 0 to EXCLUDE the concept itself.

snippets.headline: Qualifying diagnosis records are reduced to one lowest-code diabetes diagnosis per patient before adherence analysis.
snippets.content: The diagnosis rollup from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx` groups by `patient_id` and selects `MIN(icd10_code) AS dx_code`. In the version with onset timing, it first applies `(icd10_code LIKE 'E11%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E10%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E13%') AND onset_date <= DATE'2026-12-31'`. That version defines the description as `min_by(description, icd10_code)`, meaning `dx_desc` is the description of the selected lowest code; other statements use `MIN(description)` independently, which is a different description-selection rule and should not be silently substituted when code-description pairing matters.

snippets.headline: Retinopathy status identifies patients with documented E11.319 onset on or before the specified October 30, 2026 as-of date.
snippets.content: The selected `retinopathy` flag is true when the patient appears in the distinct patient set from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition` satisfying `icd10_code = 'E11.319'` and `onset_date <= DATE'2026-10-30'`; otherwise it is false for retained adherence rows. The condition set is deduplicated by `patient_id`, so multiple qualifying condition records still produce one status match per patient. This query-supported definition answers whether the patient has documented E11.319 by the stated as-of date, not whether the patient has any other retinopathy code or a later onset.

snippets.headline: Diabetes eligibility follows diagnosis descendants under three ICD categories, while screening for antipsychotic users uses a different clinical cohort.
snippets.content: The diabetes cohort is defined by subsumption over the ICD-10-CM hierarchy under E10, E11, and E13, rather than only exact matches to those three codes. SSD means Diabetes Screening for People on Antipsychotics and uses a separate cohort: serious mental illness plus antipsychotic dispensing, ages 18–64. Its numerator is a glucose or HbA1c screen, not diabetes-cohort membership. SSD patient-level screening gaps INCLUDE rows in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ssd where evidence_datetime IS NULL.

snippets.headline: Cardiorenal patients have diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure diagnoses documented through specified diagnosis-code families.
snippets.content: A cardiorenal patient is defined by all three diagnosis flags being present in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition for the same patient_id: at least one icd10_code LIKE 'E10%', 'E11%', or 'E13%' for diabetes, at least one icd10_code LIKE 'N18%' for chronic kidney disease, and at least one icd10_code LIKE 'I50%' for heart failure. Each flag is computed with MAX(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) grouped by patient_id, and the final cohort requires has_dm = 1 AND has_ckd = 1 AND has_hf = 1. These diagnosis families are inclusion criteria for the cardiorenal cohort, not merely descriptive labels.

snippets.headline: Full cardiorenal regimen status requires recorded statin, ACE inhibitor or ARB, and SGLT2 orders, without requiring current supply.
snippets.content: Build the cardiorenal patient set from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition through icd10_code membership in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure.descendant_code, intersecting diabetes ancestors IN ('E10','E11','E13'), kidney disease ancestor 'N18', and heart failure ancestor 'I50'. For eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.care_order_med, classify rxnorm_code through membership in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure.descendant_code: INCLUDE ancestor 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' for on_statin, ancestors IN ('DRUGCLASS-ACE','DRUGCLASS-ARB') for on_ace_arb, and ancestor 'DRUGCLASS-SGLT2' for on_sglt2. Each flag is MAX(CASE WHEN membership THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) GROUP BY patient_id. LEFT JOIN the cohort to these medication aggregates ON patient_id = patient_id and convert absent flags with COALESCE(flag,0)=1, preserving patients without medication records. Full status is COALESCE(on_statin,0)=1 AND COALESCE(on_ace_arb,0)=1 AND COALESCE(on_sglt2,0)=1; 'on_full_triad' and 'on_full_cardiorenal_regimen' implement the same definition. No start_ts or stop_ts filters constrain these historical-order flags. Membership tests avoid closure fanout, and patient-level aggregation on both sides avoids multiplying cohort rows; joining raw conditions directly to raw orders would not preserve this grain.

snippets.headline: Statin adherence patient details link diabetes hierarchy roots and most recent statin orders through patient identity and terminology closure mappings.
snippets.content: Correlate eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_spd s to eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition dx ON dx.patient_id = s.patient_id within scalar aggregate subqueries. INNER JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure cl ON cl.descendant_code = dx.icd10_code AND cl.ancestor_code IN ('E10','E11','E13'), including onset_date <= D for the diagnosis-code selection, and compute MIN(dx.icd10_code). The root selection uses MIN(cl.ancestor_code) with no onset bound in this variant; the independently minimized root is not guaranteed to belong to the selected minimum diagnosis. Correlate s.patient_id to eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med m.patient_id, INNER JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure c ON c.descendant_code = m.rxnorm_code AND c.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN', and compute MAX(start_ts) and max_by(description,start_ts) without a time cutoff. Scalar aggregates preserve the gold row with NULL when no match exists and avoid join fanout; multiple diagnoses and closure ancestors are reduced by the aggregates. Scope the gold row by patient_id and measurement_year, and do not equate unrestricted last order start with the gold evidence_datetime.

snippets.headline: The cardio-renal diabetes cohort includes patients with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure diagnoses together.
snippets.content: The cardio-renal diabetes cohort is defined from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx at the distinct `patient_id` grain. A patient is INCLUDED only when they have at least one diagnosis code matching each of these three required groups: diabetes `icd10_code LIKE 'E11%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E10%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E13%'`, chronic kidney disease `icd10_code LIKE 'N18%'`, and heart failure `icd10_code LIKE 'I50%'`. The cohort construction uses INNER JOINs among the three distinct patient lists, so missing any one group excludes the patient. Because the diagnosis table can contain multiple encounter rows per patient, deduplicate to `SELECT DISTINCT patient_id` for each condition group before joining or aggregating.

snippets.headline: Clinic adherence records connect to complications through patient identity, while diagnosis codes connect to ancestors through closure descendants.
snippets.content: Build the complete relationship path as follows: first select distinct `patient_id, clinic_id` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_protocol_adherence`; separately join `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition` to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure` with the INNER JOIN condition `cl.descendant_code = c.icd10_code`; then left join the deduplicated complication patients to adherence rows with `dm.patient_id = comp.patient_id` (the query uses `USING (patient_id)`). The INNER JOIN requires a matching closure row and the ancestor-code filter removes nonqualifying diagnoses; the LEFT JOIN preserves every adherence patient-clinic row, assigning null for patients without a qualifying complication. Deduplication of both the adherence patient-clinic pairs and complication patients prevents repeated source rows from inflating the clinic-level average, although one patient can still appear once per clinic.

snippets.headline: Diabetes quality reporting covers five HEDIS aligned demonstration measures, with patient evidence tables and governed views for rates.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: This supplied portion describes GSD, KED, BPD, SPD and EED as HEDIS-aligned demonstration measures, not NCQA-certified measures. Each has a patient-level gold_adherence_<measure> table for detail and care gaps and a corresponding compliance_metrics view for rates. The metric views expose Measurement Year, Compliance Status, Age Band and Measure dimensions; MET / NOT_MET logic resides in Compliance Status. The diabetes cohort uses subsumption over the ICD-10-CM hierarchy under E10/E11/E13.

snippets.headline: The E11.22 patient count, dual-adherence count, and additional N18 coding count answer different cohort questions.
snippets.content: In `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx`, build one diagnosis row per patient using `MIN(icd10_code) FILTER (WHERE onset_date <= DATE'2026-12-31')` over codes matching `icd10_code LIKE 'E1%'`, then retain `dxmin.prim = 'E11.22'`. `count(*)` measures the resulting E11.22 diagnosis rows, while `count_if(ked.patient_id IS NOT NULL AND spd.patient_id IS NOT NULL)` measures rows having a match in both `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked` and `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_spd`. Separately, `count_if(ckd.patient_id IS NOT NULL)` measures E11.22 rows also matching a distinct patient set from `bronze_pat_enc_dx` where `icd10_code LIKE 'N18%'`. These are not interchangeable: the first is the E11.22 cohort, the second is dual-table coverage, and the third is additional N18 coding; because the adherence CTEs are not deduplicated, duplicate patient rows there can inflate counts after the left joins.

snippets.headline: Diagnosis complications are classified into kidney, retinopathy, neuropathy, circulatory, or uncomplicated categories using code-pattern precedence.
snippets.content: The complication bucket is derived from the selected `dx_code` using this complete CASE mapping: `dx_code LIKE 'E1_.2%'` maps to `'kidney'`; `dx_code LIKE 'E1_.3%'` maps to `'retinopathy'`; `dx_code LIKE 'E1_.4%'` maps to `'neuropathy'`; `dx_code LIKE 'E1_.5%'` maps to `'circulatory'`; all other values map to `'uncomplicated'`. Because the CASE evaluates top to bottom, the first matching pattern determines `cx_bucket`. The classification is applied after the patient-level diagnosis reduction from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx` and the adherence join to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd`.

snippets.headline: Text-based cardiorenal membership searches diagnosis descriptions but still requires all three clinical conditions.
snippets.content: A description-based cardiorenal cohort uses text matching in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition instead of ICD hierarchy matching. INCLUDE diabetes patients with `lower(description) LIKE '%diabetes%'`, chronic kidney disease patients with `lower(description) LIKE '%chronic kidney%' OR lower(description) LIKE '%ckd%'`, and heart failure patients with `lower(description) LIKE '%heart failure%'`. The cohort is still the intersection of all three distinct `patient_id` sets, joined on `patient_id`. This text-based rule is a separate cohort construction method from ICD-prefix or ICD-closure rules and can return different patients when descriptions and codes do not align.

snippets.headline: Kidney evaluation requires both kidney tests, while the urine test only gap identifies patients whose blood test is already complete.
snippets.content: KED, Kidney Health Evaluation, covers diabetics aged 18–85 and requires BOTH an eGFR and a uACR test. In eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked, KED gaps INCLUDE NOT (gold_adherence_ked.egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND gold_adherence_ked.uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL), equivalent to egfr_datetime IS NULL OR uacr_datetime IS NULL. The care-gap count is COUNT_IF(NOT (gold_adherence_ked.egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND gold_adherence_ked.uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL)). The narrower 'uACR gap' or 'close the uACR gap' filter INCLUDES gold_adherence_ked.egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND gold_adherence_ked.uacr_datetime IS NULL. The text identifies uACR as usually the limiting component and uses Gap Reason to explain KED gaps.

snippets.headline: Step-3 follow-up adherence counts closed ninety-day windows, while open obligations identify high-A1c patients still actionable during the year.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: Protocol Step-3 means A1c follow-up after a high result and uses eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.protocol_adherence_metrics. It counts only closed 90-day follow-up windows, with Trigger Events as the denominator. Open Obligations identify high-A1c patients still closable this year and are surfaced for action questions. Recent months are not described as a decline because their windows are not yet closed.

snippets.headline: Protocol Step Three expects an A1c recheck or therapy change within ninety days after an A1c at or above target.
snippets.source: Care Protocol — Protocol Process & Medication Adherence (ect)
snippets.content: Protocol Step 3 begins after an A1c at/above target and expects a recheck A1c or therapy change within 90 days. eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_protocol_adherence has one row per high-A1c trigger, with clinic_id and panel_id. Trigger month is DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', gold_protocol_adherence.trigger_ts).

snippets.headline: Blood sugar compliance includes moderate control, whereas good control and poor control apply different thresholds across all eligible patients.
snippets.content: GSD, Glycemic Status Assessment, covers diabetics aged 18–75 and uses the last A1c of the measurement year in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd. GSD compliance, also called Blood Sugar Controlled, GSD rate, or blood sugar controlled rate, is COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value <= 9.0) / COUNT(*). Good Control Rate, also called good glycemic control or controlled diabetes, is COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value < 8.0) / COUNT(*). Poor Control Rate, also called poor glycemic control or uncontrolled diabetes, is COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value > 9.0 OR gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_datetime IS NULL) / COUNT(*). Each denominator is all eligible patient rows in the selected scope, not only tested patients; missing tests are not compliant. Compliance and good control answer different questions because the former includes A1c values from 8.0 through 9.0.

snippets.headline: Elevated glycemic trigger events are patient measurements above nine with follow-up assessed during the subsequent ninety days.
snippets.content: For calendar year 2025, a trigger event is an HbA1c observation whose modeled-or-raw value is `> 9` and whose description does NOT match the case-insensitive regular expression `recheck`. The value is `CASE WHEN g.glycemic_poor AND g.modeled_a1c IS NOT NULL THEN g.modeled_a1c ELSE o.value_num END`, so a non-null modeled value replaces the raw observation value only for patients flagged `glycemic_poor`. HbA1c observations are identified by joining `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation o` to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts lp` on `o.loinc_code = lp.loinc_code` with `lp.part = 'LP-HBA1C' AND lp.predicate = 'has_component'`. The year scope is `year(o.result_ts) = 2025`.

snippets.headline: A1c testing measures evidence availability across eligible patients, and glycemic bands separate untested, good, poor, and moderate results.
snippets.content: A1c testing rate is COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL) / COUNT(*) on eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd, with all eligible patient rows as denominator. It answers whether testing occurred, rather than whether the A1c met a control threshold. The glycemic band expression is CASE WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_datetime IS NULL THEN 'Not tested' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value < 8.0 THEN 'Good (<8%)' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value > 9.0 THEN 'Poor (>9%)' ELSE 'Moderate (8-9%)' END. Missing evidence takes precedence over numeric bands.

snippets.headline: Raw A1c detail returns the twenty most recent component-matched results with timestamps, codes, numeric values, and units.
snippets.content: For individual A1c result values over time, use `SELECT result_ts, loinc_code, value_num, units FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_lab_result WHERE component = 'Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total' ORDER BY result_ts DESC LIMIT 20`. The filter direction is INCLUDE for the exact component value `'Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total'`. The query returns at most 20 rows, ordered from newest to oldest by `result_ts`, and is intended for patient-level result detail rather than aggregated metric-view measures.

snippets.headline: High A1c evidence counts distinguish all qualifying records from observation-backed records and records also linked to protocol triggers.
snippets.content: High A1c evidence coverage uses `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd g` with `g.evidence_value > 9.0`, INNER JOINed by `patient_id` to a one-row-per-patient rollup from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx` restricted to `icd10_code LIKE 'E1%'`; the rollup calculates `MIN(icd10_code) FILTER (WHERE onset_date <= DATE'2026-12-31') AS prim`, but does not require `prim` to be non-null. Observation support is a correlated `count(*)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation o` where `o.patient_id = g.patient_id AND o.result_ts = g.evidence_datetime AND o.value_num = g.evidence_value`, producing `matches`. Protocol-trigger support is a correlated `count(*)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_protocol_adherence p` where `p.patient_id = g.patient_id AND p.trigger_ts = g.evidence_datetime`, producing `is_trigger`; no direct observation-to-protocol join is used. The jointly reported measures are `count(*) poor`, `count_if(matches > 0) observed`, and `count_if(matches > 0 AND is_trigger > 0) observed_trigger`, all at the retained adherence-row grain, not distinct-patient grain. Multiple observation or protocol matches do not multiply adherence rows because they are counted in scalar subqueries; replacing these with raw joins would risk fanout. Unlike the eligible status population, this population has no `measurement_year` or `eligible_flag` restriction and includes the broader diagnosis pattern `'E1%'`.

snippets.headline: The patient roster provides both a poor-glycemic flag and modeled HbA1c values used to characterize the 2025 patient panel.
snippets.content: The roster-level counts are `(SELECT count(*) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.panel_roster WHERE glycemic_poor)` for patients flagged poor glycemic control and `(SELECT count(*) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.panel_roster WHERE glycemic_poor AND modeled_a1c > 9)` for poor-glycemic patients whose modeled HbA1c exceeds 9. These are row counts from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.panel_roster`, not distinct patient counts, because the SQL uses `count(*)` rather than `count(DISTINCT patient_id)`. Use the first count for roster rows marked `glycemic_poor`; use the second for rows satisfying both `glycemic_poor` and `modeled_a1c > 9`.

snippets.headline: HEDIS diabetes quality uses five deterministic measures to assess eligible patients in synthetic, Epic-shaped data.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] HEDIS Diabetes Quality — Care Protocol (dev).lvdash.json
snippets.content: The care protocol evaluates five HEDIS-aligned diabetes measures from synthetic, Epic-shaped data: GSD for glycemic status and A1c testing, KED for kidney health evaluation, BPD for blood-pressure control, SPD for statin therapy, and EED for diabetic eye examination. The population is described as 25,000 patients, but each measure's denominator is its own eligible-patient population. The data is explicitly not NCQA-certified and not for clinical use.

snippets.headline: This metric view measures whether high A1c results receive timely follow-up, revealing protocol adherence by clinic and primary-care panel.
snippets.content: `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.protocol_adherence_metrics` is a Diabetes care-protocol Step 3 metrics view. The business question is whether an A1c result >= 9% (poor control) receives a follow-up A1c within 90 days; it is HEDIS-aligned for demonstration and is not NCQA-certified. Query the exposed dimensions and measures from this metrics view rather than treating it as a raw-row table, and use `MEASURE()` for every measure with `GROUP BY ALL`. Its underlying source is `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_protocol_adherence` (ASSET).

snippets.headline: Good and poor glycemic control rates measure tested patients, whereas glycemic assessment compliance measures testing among all eligible patients.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: On eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd, good control is COUNT_IF(evidence_value < 8.0) / COUNT_IF(evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL), and poor control is COUNT_IF(evidence_value > 9.0) / COUNT_IF(evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL). Both denominators count A1c-tested patient rows, unlike GSD compliance's COUNT(*) eligible-row denominator. Average latest A1c (%) is AVG(evidence_value); the supplied expression has no explicit evidence_datetime filter. The clinic example also reports COUNT(*) AS eligible_patients and COUNT_IF(evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL) / COUNT(*) AS gsd_compliance_rate, GROUP BY clinic_id ORDER BY gsd_compliance_rate DESC, without a year filter. The verified poor-control sample uses MEASURE(`Poor Control Rate`) from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics. The poorly controlled patient filter INCLUDES evidence_value > 9.0.

snippets.headline: Glycemic assessment compliance measures annual testing among eligible diabetic adults, rather than whether their blood sugar is controlled.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: GSD means Glycemic Status Assessment: diabetics aged 18-75 with an A1c test in the measurement year. Patient-level clinic/panel compliance is COUNT_IF(evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL) / COUNT(*) over eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd, with all patient rows in the breakdown as denominator. Care gaps INCLUDE evidence_datetime IS NULL. This testing rate differs from good and poor control rates, whose denominator is A1c-tested patients rather than all eligible patient rows.

snippets.headline: The average A1c result is calculated within the hemoglobin A1c concept rather than across mixed laboratory analytes.
snippets.content: Use `SELECT MEASURE(`Average Result`) AS avg_a1c FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.lab_result_metrics WHERE `Lab Concept` = 'Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total'` for the agent's average A1c query. The exact concept filter is required by the curated instruction. The underlying raw-result measure is `AVG(gold_lab_result.value_num)`, but the supplied A1c query uses the governed metric view and its `MEASURE()` interface.

snippets.headline: Patient-level A1c results classify patients into no-result, good-control, poor-control, or intermediate-control bands.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: The patient-level GSD A1c control band is derived from `gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value`. Use this exact expression: `CASE WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value IS NULL THEN 'No A1c' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value < 8 THEN 'Good control (<8%)' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value > 9 THEN 'Poor control (>9%)' ELSE '8-9%' END`. A missing value means `No A1c`; values below 8 are `Good control (<8%)`; values above 9 are `Poor control (>9%)`; all remaining non-null values, including 8 and 9, are `8-9%`.

snippets.headline: Clinic protocol adherence is ranked by Step-3 A1c follow-up rate, with open obligations and follow-up timing reported alongside.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For clinic-level Step-3 A1c follow-up adherence, query `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.protocol_adherence_metrics` and select `Clinic`, `MEASURE(``Trigger Events``) AS closed_triggers`, `MEASURE(``Followed Up In Time``) AS followed_up`, `MEASURE(``Protocol Step 3 Adherence Rate``) AS step3_adherence_rate`, `MEASURE(``Open Obligations``) AS open_obligations`, and `MEASURE(``Avg Days To Follow-up``) AS avg_days_to_followup`. Group by `Clinic` and order by `step3_adherence_rate` ascending to identify clinics with the lowest adherence. The same result reports trigger events, timely follow-ups, open obligations, and average days to follow-up for each clinic.

snippets.headline: Raw HbA1c thresholds and modeled trigger thresholds answer different patient-identification questions and must not be treated as interchangeable.
snippets.content: The 2025 HbA1c comparison exposes three distinct patient counts. `raw_trig_ge7_pts` counts distinct patients with raw `value_num >= 7`; `raw_trig_gt9_pts` counts distinct patients with raw `value_num > 9`; and `modeled_trig_gt9_pts` counts distinct patients where `coalesce(CASE WHEN r.glycemic_poor AND r.modeled_a1c IS NOT NULL THEN r.modeled_a1c ELSE a.value_num END,0) > 9`. The modeled count uses the panel roster only for the replacement rule and is therefore not equivalent to either raw threshold count. All three counts exclude observations whose descriptions match `lower(coalesce(o.description,'')) RLIKE 'recheck'` and scope observations to `year(o.result_ts)=2025`.

snippets.headline: Five diabetes quality measures evaluate glycemic testing, kidney evaluation, blood-pressure control, statin therapy, and diabetic eye examinations.
snippets.content: The HEDIS-aligned diabetes quality protocol contains five deterministic measures over a synthetic 25,000-patient, Epic-shaped population: GSD (glycemic status/A1c testing), KED (kidney health evaluation), BPD (blood-pressure control), SPD (statin therapy), and EED (diabetic eye exam). The protocol describes each rate as the share of eligible diabetes patients who met that measure. The data is synthetic, not NCQA-certified, and not intended for clinical use.

snippets.headline: Medication adherence covers adults with at least two metformin fills, and adherence requires medication coverage of at least eighty percent.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: MAD covers adults with at least two biguanide (metformin) fills; adherent means PDC >= 80 percent. The clinic query uses eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.mad_compliance_metrics with MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`), MEASURE(`Adherent Patients`), MEASURE(`MAD Adherence Rate`), and MEASURE(`Avg PDC`). The general latest-year default and the six-measure comparison use the GSD gold table for MAD's latest year.

These are the care-protocol knowledge edges, one sentence per edge. They are the same facts the knowledge graph
and `protocol_edges` hold: this Page is generated from `src/terminology/protocol_edges.csv` (`scripts/gen_protocol_pages.py`), so it can't drift from them. Synthetic demo protocol; not clinical guidance.

## Drug-class recommendations

- Statins are recommended for the SPD measure (statin therapy, ages 40-75). *(protocol section CP-DM-2025.1 sec2/sec6)*
- ACE inhibitors are recommended for albuminuria. *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- ARBs are recommended for albuminuria. *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended for chronic kidney disease (value set `COMORBID_CKD`). *(protocol section CP sec3)*
- SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended for heart failure (value set `COMORBID_HF`). *(protocol section CP sec3)*
- Metformin (biguanide) is first-line for glucose lowering. *(protocol section CP-GLY-2)*

## Contraindications

- Statins are contraindicated with pregnancy (value set `CONTRA_PREGNANCY`). *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- Statins are contraindicated with active hepatic disease (value set `CONTRA_HEPATIC`). *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- ACE inhibitors are contraindicated with pregnancy (value set `CONTRA_PREGNANCY`). *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- ARBs are contraindicated with pregnancy (value set `CONTRA_PREGNANCY`). *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- Metformin (biguanide) is contraindicated when eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73m². *(protocol section CP-GLY-2)*
- SGLT2 inhibitors are contraindicated when eGFR below 20 mL/min/1.73m². *(protocol section CP sec4)*

## What each measure is monitored by

- GSD is monitored by HbA1c (LOINC part LP-HBA1C). *(protocol section CP sec5)*
- KED is monitored by eGFR (LP-EGFR). *(protocol section CP sec5)*
- KED is monitored by uACR (LP-UACR). *(protocol section CP sec5)*
- BPD is monitored by systolic blood pressure (LP-SBP). *(protocol section CP sec5)*
- BPD is monitored by diastolic blood pressure (LP-DBP). *(protocol section CP sec5)*

## Thresholds and definitions

- Albuminuria is defined by uACR of 30 mg/g or more. *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- BPD has the threshold systolic below 140 mmHg. *(protocol section CP sec2)*
- BPD has the threshold diastolic below 90 mmHg. *(protocol section CP sec2)*
- GSD has the threshold good control: A1c below 8%. *(protocol section CP sec2)*
- GSD has the threshold poor control: A1c above 9%. *(protocol section CP sec3)*

## Which lab each threshold is measured on

- Good control: A1c below 8% is measured on HbA1c (LOINC part LP-HBA1C). *(protocol section CP sec2)*
- Poor control: A1c above 9% is measured on HbA1c (LOINC part LP-HBA1C). *(protocol section CP sec3)*
- eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73m² is measured on eGFR (LP-EGFR). *(protocol section CP-GLY-2)*
- eGFR below 20 mL/min/1.73m² is measured on eGFR (LP-EGFR). *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- uACR of 30 mg/g or more is measured on uACR (LP-UACR). *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- Systolic below 140 mmHg is measured on systolic blood pressure (LP-SBP). *(protocol section CP sec2)*
- Diastolic below 90 mmHg is measured on diastolic blood pressure (LP-DBP). *(protocol section CP sec2)*

For the A1c recheck rule (Protocol Step 3) see the Page *Protocol Step 3 — A1c recheck within 90 days*.

**Related assets:** `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges`, `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment`

## The care protocol (v2025.1) does not define an A1c target for older adults with moderate comorbidity

The protocol's A1c thresholds are **uniform across all adults** — there is no individualized target based on age or comorbidity level. [Care-protocol rules (drug classes, contraindications, thresholds)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/e210469b-4179-45be-91f3-398359a04af3?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/23e2b454fc9b488a97c8a8b644d5f3d5?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_b9f439)

### A1c thresholds the protocol does define

| Rule | Threshold | Protocol Section |
|---|---|---|
| Good glycemic control (GSD) | A1c **< 8%** | CP sec2 |
| Poor glycemic control (GSD) | A1c **> 9%** | CP sec3 |
| Step 3 follow-up trigger | A1c ≥ 9% → recheck within **90 days** | CP sec3 / Step 3 |

These apply identically to every eligible diabetic patient (ages 18–75). [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-788eac61-11a7-482a-9d5c-eac964e04174)

### What was checked

I reviewed all **29 protocol rules** in the `protocol_edges` knowledge graph. [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/protocol_edges?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) The only rule tagged with version identifier "CP-DM-2025.1" (section sec2/sec6) recommends **statins for SPD** — it does not address A1c. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/23e2b454fc9b488a97c8a8b644d5f3d5?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_b9f439) No rule references "older adult," "elderly," "comorbidity," or any age-stratified glycemic goal. The glossary pages for A1c and Protocol Step 3 likewise contain no age- or comorbidity-based differentiation. [Protocol Step 3 — A1c recheck within 90 days](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/240387f5-7f44-4dc6-9e12-08e037f2d00d?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [HbA1c (A1c) — Hemoglobin A1c](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/198bc1a7-dbd0-4ab8-a66e-d83cc4e95e59?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

### Bottom line

The closest answer is **< 8%** (the protocol's general "good control" threshold), but this is not a target set specifically for older patients with moderate comorbidity — it applies to everyone. If your v2025.1 protocol document includes an age/comorbidity-stratified target, that rule has not been loaded into this dataset.

> **Note:** This is a synthetic, HEDIS-aligned demo protocol and is **not** NCQA-certified or intended for clinical use. genie_one_sql: SELECT * FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`protocol_edges` ORDER BY `predicate`, `subject`

queries: eGFR LOINC codes HEDIS measures measurement year 2026 kidney estimated glomerular filtration rate

snippets.headline: eGFR results include raw LOINC codes linked to component part LP-EGFR through the terminology table.
snippets.content: To include eGFR results in `gold_lab_result`, use `gold_lab_result.loinc_code IN (SELECT loinc_code FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts WHERE predicate = 'has_component' AND part = 'LP-EGFR')`. The filter direction is INCLUDE, with the complete component value `'LP-EGFR'` and predicate `'has_component'`. The agent's sample question for which codes count as eGFR uses the same predicate and part values.

snippets.headline: Cross-year kidney evaluation comparisons can show an artificial decrease when later-year kidney test value sets retain only CKD-EPI evidence.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: A later measurement year's KED eGFR value set keeps only the CKD-EPI code. Cross-year KED comparisons can consequently show an artificial drop. The content provides no literal LOINC code or specific later year for this caveat.

snippets.headline: KED compliance measures kidney-health testing for eligible diabetes patients aged 18 through 85 during each measurement year.
snippets.content: `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics` is a HEDIS-aligned demonstration metrics view for Kidney Health Evaluation (KED), not an NCQA-certified measure. Its denominator is eligible diabetes patients aged 18-85, and full compliance requires BOTH an eGFR test and a uACR test in the measurement year. Query measures from the metrics view with `MEASURE()` and `GROUP BY ALL`; do not treat the view as an ordinary row-level table or reconstruct its measures with `SUM`/`COUNT`.

snippets.headline: eGFR method breakdown compares observation and patient volume for the glomerular filtration rate predicted concept.
snippets.content: For eGFR results by assay, use `SELECT `Method`, MEASURE(`Observations`) AS results, MEASURE(`Patients Tested`) AS patients FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.lab_result_metrics WHERE `Lab Concept` = 'Glomerular filtration rate.predicted' GROUP BY `Method` ORDER BY results DESC`. The output grain is one row per `Method` within the exact concept `'Glomerular filtration rate.predicted'`. It reports both result observations and distinct patients, ordered by observations descending.

snippets.headline: Kidney evaluation performance includes both kidney testing components, with urine albumin testing usually identified as the limiting component.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: KED means kidney evaluation with eGFR and uACR components. Annual performance from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics groups by `Measurement Year` and selects MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`), MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`), MEASURE(`eGFR Test Rate`), and MEASURE(`uACR Test Rate`). INCLUDE only `Measurement Year` = (SELECT MAX(measurement_year) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked). Explanations show both component rates because uACR is usually limiting. The clinic sample uses the same year filter, groups by Clinic, selects MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`) and MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`), and orders by Clinic.

snippets.headline: eGFR laboratory codes share the designated component, and their assay methods come from method Parts attached to those codes.
snippets.content: In eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts, INCLUDE predicate = 'has_component' AND part = 'LP-EGFR' to find eGFR codes here. The verified code-set output is concat_ws(',', sort_array(collect_set(loinc_code))) over that selection. For assay methods, return loinc_code, part_name AS method from the same table WHERE predicate = 'has_method' AND loinc_code IN (SELECT loinc_code FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts WHERE predicate = 'has_component' AND part = 'LP-EGFR'), ordered by loinc_code.

snippets.headline: eGFR tested patients count eligible people with at least one eGFR test during the measurement year.
snippets.content: On `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics`, `eGFR Tested Patients` counts eligible patients with a non-null eGFR test date; its definition-time expression is `COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL)`. Query the predefined measure as `MEASURE(`eGFR Tested Patients`)` with `GROUP BY ALL`, for example: `SELECT `Measurement Year`, MEASURE(`eGFR Tested Patients`) AS `egfr_tested_patients` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_semantic`.`ked_compliance_metrics` GROUP BY ALL`. This is the eGFR component count, not the full KED numerator.

snippets.headline: eGFR and uACR test rates are separate component measures, while KED compliance requires both tests together.
snippets.content: Two component rates answer separate questions from the full KED rate. `eGFR Test Rate` measures the share with an eGFR test and is queried as `MEASURE(`eGFR Test Rate`)`; its definition-time formula is `MEASURE(`eGFR Tested Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)`. `uACR Test Rate` measures the share with a uACR test and is queried as `MEASURE(`uACR Test Rate`)`; its definition-time formula is `MEASURE(`uACR Tested Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)`. The full-measure question instead uses `MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`)`, which requires both tests and cannot be replaced by either component rate; query selected measures with dimensions and `GROUP BY ALL`.

snippets.headline: The measure dimension identifies KED as the HEDIS kidney-health evaluation measure represented by this metrics view.
snippets.content: The exposed dimension `Measure` is mapped from source `measure_id` and identifies the HEDIS measure code; this view reports KED, meaning Kidney Health Evaluation. Query the exposed dimension `` `Measure` `` when results need an explicit measure label, rather than relying only on the asset name. Example: `SELECT `Measure`, MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`) AS `ked_compliance_rate` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_semantic`.`ked_compliance_metrics` GROUP BY ALL`.

snippets.headline: Each KED eGFR value-set version connects to observed patients through matching LOINC codes in the clinical observation records.
snippets.content: The complete relationship path for eGFR code matching is `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment` filtered by `segment_id = 'KED_EGFR'` -> `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment.code` equals `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation.loinc_code` -> observation patients via `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation.patient_id`. The SQL first derives distinct versions from `measurement_year`, then joins the version-and-code rows back on `measurement_year`, and finally LEFT JOINs observations on `loinc_code`; unmatched versions remain present with zero matching patients. Multiple code rows can match one version and multiple observations can match one code, so use `COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id)` rather than counting joined rows to avoid code- and observation-level fanout.

snippets.headline: Clinic-specific kidney gap lists use measurement year 2026, clinic CLINIC-08, and ascending eGFR with nulls first.
snippets.content: For KED gap-detail rows in this example scope, filter `measurement_year = 2026 AND clinic_id = 'CLINIC-08' AND (egfr_datetime IS NULL OR uacr_datetime IS NULL)`. Select `patient_id`, `age`, `egfr_value`, `egfr_datetime`, and `uacr_datetime`. Order by `egfr_value ASC NULLS FIRST`, so missing eGFR values appear before measured values and lower eGFR values appear first.

snippets.headline: Curated HEDIS value set membership depends on measurement year, because the same segment can contain different codes across versions.
snippets.content: eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment stores member codes with segment_id, code_system, and measurement_year. Stated segment examples are 'GSD_A1C_TEST', 'KED_EGFR', and 'SPD_STATIN'; stated code systems are 'LOINC', 'ICD10CM', and 'RXNORM'. The same segment_id can have different members across measurement years, so current-qualification questions must consider measurement_year. The MY2025 / '2025 value set' filter INCLUDES measurement_year = 2025; the MY2026 / '2026 value set' filter INCLUDES measurement_year = 2026. Available value sets are listed as DISTINCT segment_id, segment_name, owner ordered by segment_id.

snippets.headline: Kidney evaluation requires both kidney tests, while the urine test only gap identifies patients whose blood test is already complete.
snippets.content: KED, Kidney Health Evaluation, covers diabetics aged 18–85 and requires BOTH an eGFR and a uACR test. In eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked, KED gaps INCLUDE NOT (gold_adherence_ked.egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND gold_adherence_ked.uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL), equivalent to egfr_datetime IS NULL OR uacr_datetime IS NULL. The care-gap count is COUNT_IF(NOT (gold_adherence_ked.egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND gold_adherence_ked.uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL)). The narrower 'uACR gap' or 'close the uACR gap' filter INCLUDES gold_adherence_ked.egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND gold_adherence_ked.uacr_datetime IS NULL. The text identifies uACR as usually the limiting component and uses Gap Reason to explain KED gaps.

snippets.headline: Laboratory result analysis uses governed measures grouped by LOINC concepts, with separate sources for patient detail and terminology structure.
snippets.content: This Genie Agent covers laboratory result test volume, patients tested, and result values using the governed view `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.lab_result_metrics`. The view groups results by LOINC multiaxial concepts, including component, system, and method. Use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_lab_result` for individual patient-level values over time and `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts` for LOINC code and method structure. The data is synthetic and HEDIS-aligned for demonstration, not NCQA-certified or for clinical use.

snippets.headline: eGFR patient coverage counts distinct observed patients matched to each version of the KED eGFR code set during 2025.
snippets.content: The eGFR patient-coverage measure counts `COUNT(DISTINCT o.patient_id)` for observations in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation` where `YEAR(result_ts) = 2025`, grouped by value-set version. The matched observation codes are collected as a comma-separated distinct set with `concat_ws(', ', collect_set(o.loinc_code))`; this is a code-coverage result, not a count of observations. Value-set versions come from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment` filtered with `segment_id = 'KED_EGFR'`, and each version is retained even when no 2025 patients match because the final joins are LEFT JOINs.

snippets.headline: Average, minimum, and maximum laboratory results are valid only within one analyte concept or one specific LOINC code.
snippets.content: Use `MEASURE(`Average Result`)`, minimum, or maximum only after constraining results to a single `Lab Concept` or a single `LOINC Code`. The agent explicitly warns that units differ across analytes, such as A1c in `%`, eGFR in `mL/min`, and blood pressure in `mmHg`. For average raw values, the reusable expression is `AVG(gold_lab_result.value_num)`. The A1c example filters `WHERE `Lab Concept` = 'Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total'` before selecting `MEASURE(`Average Result`)`.

snippets.headline: Compliance status distinguishes patients meeting both kidney-testing requirements from those missing at least one test.
snippets.content: The exposed dimension `Compliance Status` is computed live from the source test dates: definition-time expression `CASE WHEN egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'MET' ELSE 'NOT_MET' END`. `MET` means both an eGFR and a uACR test were found in the measurement year; `NOT_MET` means at least one is missing. The complete value set is `'MET'` and `'NOT_MET'`; filter or group the exposed dimension `` `Compliance Status` `` when reporting compliant versus noncompliant patients.

snippets.headline: KED compliance rate measures the share of eligible diabetes patients receiving both required kidney tests.
snippets.content: On `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics`, `KED Compliance Rate` answers the full-measure question: what share of eligible diabetes patients completed both eGFR and uACR testing? Its definition-time formula is `MEASURE(`Compliant Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)`, and the queryable expression is exactly `MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`)`. Query it at the desired dimension grain, such as `SELECT `Clinic`, MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`) AS `ked_compliance_rate` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_semantic`.`ked_compliance_metrics` GROUP BY ALL`; do not wrap this measure in another aggregate.

snippets.headline: KED measures kidney health evaluation using both eGFR and uACR testing requirements for eligible diabetes patients.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] HEDIS Diabetes Quality — Care Protocol (dev).lvdash.json
snippets.content: The business term `KED` means kidney health evaluation. For rows where `gold_adherence_ked.status = 'NOT_MET'`, classify the care gap exactly as follows: when `NOT egfr_flag AND NOT uacr_flag`, use `'No eGFR and no uACR'`; when `NOT uacr_flag` otherwise, use `'No uACR test'`; otherwise use `'No eGFR test'`. The KED compliance rate is based on `AVG(CAST(numerator_flag AS INT))` across the KED eligible rows, while the gap classification uses the two component flags.

## eGFR in the Care Protocol: Measures, MY2026 Codes, and Where It's Defined

**KED (Kidney Health Evaluation) is the only quality measure that uses eGFR.** For MY2026, a single LOINC code counts: **`98979-8`** (CKD-EPI 2021). Two care-protocol medication rules also reference eGFR thresholds, but they are contraindication rules, not quality measures. [Prior eGFR analysis](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/a57cc2ab04a2425899ab01fe07da4667?o=7474653847172668)

### Where eGFR Is Used

| Context | How eGFR is used | Protocol source |
|---|---|---|
| **KED** (diabetes patients, ages 18–85) | One of two required numerator tests — a patient needs both an eGFR *and* a uACR test in the measurement year | `CP sec5`: `KED monitoredBy LP-EGFR` [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/7d933272400146bbac6d423d6cfc4148?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_521c83) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-8e0e87c6-ec71-4cc4-bc5a-cfd3232063ea) |
| **SGLT2 inhibitors** | Contraindicated when eGFR < 20 | `CP sec4`: `DRUGCLASS-SGLT2 contraindicatedWhen eGFR_LT_20` [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/7d933272400146bbac6d423d6cfc4148?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_521c83) |
| **Biguanides (Metformin)** | Contraindicated when eGFR < 30 | `CP-GLY-2`: `DRUGCLASS-BIGUANIDE contraindicatedWhen eGFR_LT_30` [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/7d933272400146bbac6d423d6cfc4148?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_521c83) |

GSD, SPD, BPD, EED, and MAD do **not** use eGFR.

### LOINC Codes That Count as eGFR, by Measurement Year

<!-- begin-embedded:query_78f627 -->
| value_set_version | segment_name | egfr_loinc_codes | code_count |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2025 | Kidney eval - eGFR (KED) | 33914-3, 98979-8 | 2 |
| 2026 | Kidney eval - eGFR (KED) [MY2026 modernized: CKD-EPI only] | 98979-8 | 1 |
<!-- end-embedded:query_78f627 -->

- **MY2025**: two codes — `33914-3` (MDRD) and `98979-8` (CKD-EPI)
- **MY2026**: one code — `98979-8` (CKD-EPI only) — the segment name explicitly says *"MY2026 modernized: CKD-EPI only"* [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/7d933272400146bbac6d423d6cfc4148?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_78f627)

### Where It's Defined

1. **Code list** — the `KED_EGFR` segment in the value-set table [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/value_set_segment?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668). Each row is tied to a `measurement_year`, so the MY2026 row carries only `98979-8`. You match lab results on `loinc_code = code` for the segment and year you want. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-edda8620-a170-4029-82f4-21a22de79a49) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-c5a7f603-0689-491a-9666-2c038996db63)
2. **Measure logic & thresholds** — the protocol-edges table [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/protocol_edges?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668), which records the `monitoredBy` and `contraindicatedWhen` relationships shown above.
3. **Glossary page** — *eGFR (Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate)* [eGFR (Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/150dfd59-85b9-4efd-8014-bb170bfe626e?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) — lists both LOINC codes and identifies eGFR as one of KED's two tests. Note: this page has **not** been updated for MY2026 and still lists `33914-3`.

### Caveat on the MY2026 Change

Dropping `33914-3` (MDRD) from the MY2026 value set could theoretically lower KED rates if the lab data still uses that code. However, in this synthetic dataset, all lab results from 2023 onward already use `98979-8` (CKD-EPI), so the change has no practical impact on MY2025 or MY2026 KED. It would only matter for historical lookbacks to 2022 or earlier. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-ed62bbb6-6537-45d5-9de2-05957f4f1f00)
